recent_decisions.decision: v0.1513.0: MP4 (H.264/AAC, and anything else Windows decodes) plays in the desktop player through Windows Media Foundation (src/media/system.rs): media::probe tries our Matroska/AV1 path first, then the system path; the decode thread and kira sound mirror the AV1 path's queue/generation/seek rules. MF's 5 functions are loaded with LoadLibraryW/GetProcAddress, never linked. Each stream counted from Windows's first sample time set to the MP4's declared start (leading empty edits of its edit list; Windows reports video 0.133 s, audio 0.021 s in the fixture where the file says 0). A critic review found and fixed: the real row layout comes only with the first picture (854/1366/portrait H.264 drew skewed), sound that truly starts late, files whose sound Windows cannot decode (sound_lost: converted with ffmpeg on screens, said on the Media page), kira's first seek made the reader on the window thread (now a no-op for a seek to 0), System32-only DLL loading. A new player shows its first picture at once (show_next_frame at open). The Media page's video got sound + Mute (media::sync_sound from the engine's audio frame sync). Card follow-ups closed on both apps.
recent_decisions.why: Operator asked how to play MP4s (2026-10-17) and said to finish the cards and pick the next best work (2026-10-18). Linking mfplat.dll would stop the app starting at all on a Windows N edition, so the functions are loaded at run time and N says the platform finding's sentence. Without the per-stream start, the picture would lag the sound by about 110 ms. Tests that are about our own decoder or the ffmpeg path turn the system decoders off on their thread (system_decoders_off_on_this_thread) because this machine's Windows plays even the VP8 fixture.
